verdict_reason: The file is deleted outright with no replacement; nothing breaks today because no code makes outbound HTTP calls, but the deletion orphans TraceIdPropagationInterceptor and leaves the CDP trace-header requirement unenforced for future clients.

todos.issue: Deleting RestClientConfig removes the only wiring of TraceIdPropagationInterceptor, which survives as an orphaned @Component (plus its test and the cdp.tracing.header-name property) whose Javadoc still claims it adds x-cdp-request-id to every outbound RestClient/RestTemplate call - it now adds it to none, so the stated CDP tracing requirement is silently unenforced for any future outbound client (the 10s connect / 30s read timeouts went with it too).
todos.fix: Finish the cleanup either way: delete TraceIdPropagationInterceptor, its test and the cdp.tracing.header-name property alongside RestClientConfig; or keep a minimal @Configuration exposing a RestClient.Builder bean with .requestInterceptor(traceIdInterceptor) and the timeouts, per best-practice section 17.
